page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6a.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor with an x86_64 architecture operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX, AES-NI, and SHA extensions, though it lacks AVX-512 extensions.

The hardware configuration features 256 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 8 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance comes with no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for persistence. Network capabilities are defined by an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. There are no discrete GPU accelerators included in this server type.

Performance benchmarks reflect consistent mid-tier execution for parallelized workloads alongside moderate single-thread compute. The instance registered a Geekbench single-core score of 1243 and a multi-core score of 9156, complemented by a PassMark CPU score of 31304.25 and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 12221.28. While cached memory bandwidth achieves 1393.35 GB/sec, uncached read and write bandwidth to large memory blocks drops to 35.41 GB/sec and 16.85 GB/sec respectively, reflecting the NUMA architecture of high-density AMD Zen 2 processors. In operational benchmarks, the instance sustained 26.09 million Redis SET operations per second and 7.52 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6a.8xlarge provides a balanced cost-efficiency profile for enterprise scenarios requiring massive memory density rather than extreme single-threaded CPU speed. Due to its large memory footprint and 32 vCPUs, it is suited for in-memory caching layers such as Redis, medium-to-large relational database hosting, real-time analytics, and data processing pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6a.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server powered by a 2.6 GHz AMD EPYC 7H12 processor on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores and 256 GB of system RAM, it maintains an 8 GB per vCPU allocation. The server includes no local disk storage and relies on network-attached storage, supported by an 8 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results show standard multi-core throughput, including a PassMark CPU score of 31304.25 and Geekbench multi-core score of 9156, alongside Redis throughput of 26.09 million SET operations per second. However, single-core throughput and uncached memory bandwidth fall on the lower end of tested instances. The instance delivers solid qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy infrastructure, making it well matched for in-memory databases, Redis deployments, enterprise application caching, and distributed data processing workloads.
